s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic mastoid area pain and swelling with recent exacerbation and a calcified mass involving the temporal bone
salient_findings: Hyperostotic lesion of the outer table of the right calvarium
Densely calcified mass involving the inferior squamosal portion of the right temporal bone
Mild patchy internal enhancement on MRI
Thickening of the inner table of the calvarium
key_facts: 28-year-old man with a history of migraine disorder
Several months of pain and swelling in the right mastoid area
Recent subjective enlargement of the mass and increased pain
Noncontrast CT showed a 3.0 × 3.0 × 1.1 cm hyperostotic lesion
MRI revealed a densely calcified mass measuring 3.6 × 1.5 × 3.0 cm
Low signal intensity on T1- and T2-weighted images
Mild patchy internal enhancement on MRI
Thickening of the inner table of the calvarium
No soft-tissue component beyond the bone or dural involvement
Laboratory studies were within normal limits

shortlist.label: Osteoma
shortlist.why_kept: Hyperostotic lesion with calcified mass involving the temporal bone

shortlist.label: Osteoblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Densely calcified mass with mild patchy internal enhancement on MRI

shortlist.label: Fibrous dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic mastoid area pain and swelling with a calcified mass

shortlist.label: Ossifying fibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Calcified mass with low signal intensity on T1- and T2-weighted images

shortlist.label: Osteoid osteoma
shortlist.why_kept: Small, calcified mass with recent subjective enlargement and increased pain

raw.rationale: The presence of a hyperostotic lesion with dense calcification and low signal intensity on T1- and T2-weighted images, along with mild patchy internal enhancement, is consistent with an osteoma. The lack of soft-tissue component or dural involvement and normal laboratory studies also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Osteoblastoma
rejected.why: Osteoblastomas are typically larger and more aggressive than the described lesion, and often have a softer tissue component.

rejected.label: Fibrous dysplasia
rejected.why: Fibrous dysplasia typically presents with a more diffuse and irregular bone lesion, and often involves multiple bones.

rejected.label: Ossifying fibroma
rejected.why: Ossifying fibromas are usually larger and have a more complex appearance on imaging, with a mix of fibrous and osseous components.

rejected.label: Osteoid osteoma
rejected.why: Osteoid osteomas are typically smaller (less than 1.5 cm) and have a characteristic nidus with surrounding sclerosis, which is not described in this case.
